title: Ahimaaz wanted to run.
paragraphs: Ahimaaz wanted to run.
That detail seems small—until you realize how dangerous it can be to desire movement without understanding the message.
In 2 Samuel 18, the battle had ended. Absalom was dead. Israel had won—but David had lost a son. Victory and grief collided in the same moment.
And someone needed to carry that news.

Ahimaaz stepped forward quickly.
Eager. Ready. Determined.
“Let me run.”

On the surface, that sounds noble.
But Joab hesitated—and that hesitation reveals something most people miss.
Because not every message is meant for every messenger.

Some messages are heavy.
Some messages require emotional strength, spiritual maturity, and the ability to carry truth without collapsing under its weight.

Ahimaaz had speed.
But he did not yet have depth.
And that tension is where this story becomes uncomfortably personal.
We live in a generation that celebrates speed.

Post it fast.
Say it first.
Be early.
Be seen.
Be heard.
But heaven does not measure readiness by urgency.
It measures it by weight-bearing capacity.
Ahimaaz insisted—and eventually, he was allowed to run.
And he ran well.

In fact, he outran the Cushite.
He arrived first.
He looked like the better messenger.
But when David asked the question that mattered most—
“Is the young man Absalom safe?”
Everything changed.

Ahimaaz answered carefully.
Vaguely.
Avoiding the full truth.
Why?

Because he had the position…
but not the preparation.

He had the moment…
but not the message.
And that is one of the most sobering realities in Scripture:
You can arrive first and still not be ready.
Let that sink in.
Because a lot of people today are arriving.

Arriving on platforms.
Arriving in influence.
Arriving in opportunities they prayed for.

But when the weight of the moment presses in…
they realize something is missing.
Depth.
Discernment.
Emotional strength.
Spiritual maturity.
Ahimaaz teaches us that passion can open doors—but only preparation sustains you inside them.
He teaches us that visibility can come before formation—and that is where many people quietly break.
Because carrying truth is not just about accuracy.

It is about delivery.
Timing.
Sensitivity.
Understanding the heart of the one receiving it.
David was not just a king waiting for a report.
He was a father waiting for news about his son.
And that changes everything.
A true messenger does not just carry information.
He carries awareness.
He carries discernment.
He carries the emotional weight of the moment.
And that is why the Cushite—though slower—was actually more prepared to deliver the full reality of what had happened.
Let that challenge you.
Because in God’s kingdom, slower does not mean lesser.

Sometimes slower means safer.
Sometimes slower means deeper.
Sometimes slower means ready.
We have to break this idea that being first is the goal.
Because in Scripture, being faithful is always more important than being fast.

Speed can get you there.
But only substance allows you to stand there.
And here is the deeper question this story asks every one of us:
What are you asking God to let you run toward… that you are not yet ready to carry?

That promotion?
That platform?
That influence?
That voice?
It is not wrong to desire it.
But it is dangerous to desire it without preparation.
Because once you arrive, the questions will come.
The weight will come.
The responsibility will come.
And in that moment, speed will not help you.
Only depth will.
This is why God often delays people—not to deny them, but to develop them.
Because the assignment is not just about getting there.
It is about carrying what is there.
And some messages—some callings—some responsibilities—require a soul that has been strengthened in private before it is revealed in public.
Ahimaaz ran with urgency.
But the message required maturity.
And that gap is where many destinies get strained.
So maybe the prayer needs to shift.

Not just:
“Lord, send me.”

But also:
“Lord, prepare me.”

Not just:
“Lord, open the door.”

But also:
“Lord, build in me the strength to stand when I walk through it.”
Because God is not just raising voices.
He is raising vessels.
And vessels must be able to carry weight without cracking.

Being chosen is powerful.
Being prepared is essential.

And sometimes the greatest mercy of God…
is not letting you run too soon.

Engagement Question:
Have you ever rushed into something you weren’t fully ready for? What did it teach you about preparation versus passion?
